front: What balance metadata does a Splay Tree store?
back: None — no heights, colors, or balance factors. Structure comes purely from rotations triggered by access (splaying).

front: Splay Tree Zig case: when does it apply, and what's the fix?
back: When node has no grandparent (its parent p is the root). Fix: a single rotation around p.

front: Splay Tree Zig-Zig case: when does it apply, and in what order do you rotate?
back: When node and its parent p are both left children (or both right children) of their respective parents. Rotate around the grandparent g FIRST, then around p.

front: Splay Tree Zig-Zag case: when does it apply, and in what order do you rotate?
back: When node is a left child and its parent p is a right child (or vice versa — opposite sides). Rotate around p FIRST, then around g.

front: Why does the rotation order differ between Zig-Zig and Zig-Zag?
back: Zig-Zig rotates the farther node (g) first, then the nearer (p) — this is what distinguishes it from two independent Zig steps, which would give a different, less balanced result. Zig-Zag rotates the nearer node (p) first since the two turns already cancel each other's direction.
Insert exactly like a plain BST insert (new node becomes a leaf), then splay(newNode) to bring it to the root.

front: Splay Tree search/find — which node gets splayed to the root, found or not?
back: Either way — the last node visited is splayed to the root: the node containing the key if found, or the last real node examined before falling off the tree if not found.

front: Splay Tree delete — first step, and what does it accomplish?
back: Call find(value), which splays the last-visited node to the root. If the key wasn't found, nothing more happens (the tree keeps the reshuffling from the failed search).

front: Splay Tree delete: the target key IS at the root after find(). What happens next?
back: Remove the root, splitting the tree into L (its left subtree) and R (its right subtree). If L is empty, R becomes the new tree. Otherwise, splay the max of L to L's root, then attach R as its right child.

front: Why can R always be attached directly as the right child of L's splayed maximum, with no further check?
back: The maximum of L has no right child by definition (it's the rightmost node) — the slot is guaranteed free.

front: What is the amortized time complexity of Splay Tree operations, and what's the worst case for a single operation?
back: Amortized O(log n) per operation (potential-function argument). A single splay can touch every node on the path to the old root — O(n) worst case for one operation.

front: Which of AVL, Red-Black, and Splay trees rotate on a pure lookup (search with no insert/delete)?
back: Only Splay trees — every access, including a plain search, triggers a splay that restructures the tree. AVL and RBT only rotate on insert/delete.
